CONTINGENCY FEE AGREEMENT

This agreement is made on April 2, 2026 between Oyelaran Law Group, a professional corporation ("the Firm"), and Marisol Oyelaran-Diaz ("the Client").

1. SCOPE OF REPRESENTATION

The Firm will represent the Client in a claim for personal injuries arising out of the ceiling collapse at 1440 Fruitvale Avenue, Oakland, California on November 14, 2025, including negotiation, filing suit if necessary, trial, and settlement. The Firm will not represent the Client on appeal, in a bankruptcy, in a related insurance coverage dispute, or in any other matter unless the parties sign a separate agreement.

2. NO GUARANTEE

The Firm has made no promise or guarantee about the outcome. Any statement by the Firm about the case is an opinion only.

3. CONTINGENCY FEE

The Client owes no fee unless a recovery is obtained. If a recovery is obtained, the Firm's fee is:

(a) 33 1/3% of the gross recovery if the matter resolves before a complaint is filed;
(b) 40% of the gross recovery if the matter resolves after a complaint is filed and before trial begins; and
(c) 45% of the gross recovery if the matter resolves after trial begins.

The fee is calculated on the gross recovery before deduction of costs. The Client understands that the fee is not set by law and is negotiable between the Firm and the Client.

4. COSTS AND EXPENSES

The Firm will advance costs and expenses, including filing fees, service fees, deposition and court reporter charges, expert witness fees, investigation, records, travel, and trial exhibits. Costs are deducted from the Client's share after the fee is calculated. The Client is responsible for costs whether or not there is a recovery, except that the Firm will waive unreimbursed costs if there is no recovery. The Firm will provide an itemized statement of costs with the settlement statement.

5. CLIENT'S RIGHTS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The Client will cooperate, keep the Firm informed of any change of address or telephone number, attend depositions and medical examinations, and respond promptly to requests for information. The Client has the sole right to accept or reject any settlement offer. The Firm will communicate every settlement offer to the Client.

6. LIENS AND SUBROGATION

The Client authorizes the Firm to satisfy from the recovery any medical lien, health plan subrogation claim, Medicare or Medi-Cal claim, or other lien the Firm determines is valid, and to hold disputed amounts in the Firm's client trust account until the dispute is resolved.

7. ASSOCIATION OF COUNSEL

The Firm may associate other counsel. The Client's total fee will not increase because of the association, and the Client's written consent is required before any division of fees with a lawyer outside the Firm.

8. DISCHARGE AND WITHDRAWAL

The Client may discharge the Firm at any time. The Firm may withdraw as permitted by the California Rules of Professional Conduct and with the court's permission if suit has been filed. If the Firm is discharged or withdraws for good cause, the Firm may assert a lien on the recovery for the reasonable value of the services rendered before the discharge or withdrawal, not to exceed the fee stated in section 3.

9. FILE

At the end of the representation the Firm will return the Client's file on request, at the Firm's expense, and will retain a copy for five years.

10. PROFESSIONAL LIABILITY INSURANCE

The Firm maintains professional liability insurance in an amount not less than $1,000,000 per claim.

11. STATUTORY NOTICE

This agreement is made under California Business and Professions Code section 6147. The Client has received a fully executed duplicate of this agreement at the time it was signed. The Client may void this agreement if it does not comply with section 6147, in which case the Firm is entitled to a reasonable fee.

12. ARBITRATION OF FEE DISPUTES

A dispute about fees or costs may be submitted to the State Bar's mandatory fee arbitration program under Business and Professions Code sections 6200 through 6206, at the Client's election. Nothing in this agreement waives that right.

13. ENTIRE AGREEMENT

This agreement is the entire agreement between the Firm and the Client on this subject and may be changed only by a writing signed by both.
